targetText: For monopoly organisations can overcome the tendency towards lowering the rate of profit by receiving monopoly superprofits at the expense of the non-trustified industries. Out of the surplus value created every year, one portion, that which has been created in the nontrustified branches of industry, is being transferred to the coowners of capitalist monopolies, whereas the share of the outsiders continually decreases. Thus the entire process drives capital beyond the frontiers of the country.
summary: Cartels and trusts restrict domestic investment to maintain monopoly superprofits, driving overaccumulated capital to seek higher returns abroad.
explanation: Bukharin explains the economic compulsion behind capital export: monopoly cartels limit domestic output to keep prices high and export their surplus capital to colonies and foreign markets.
